speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And we can also all agree that any leave enhancements will need to balance parents' caregiving needs with employers' manpower and operational needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have listened to the various proposals from various Members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We do not differ when it comes to principles, namely, that mothers are differently impacted by the arrival of a child because they need time to recuperate from childbirth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But we also agree that men should play an important role in their child's early years and that men should be encouraged to take their paternity leave and parental leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: How the leave then ought to be shared between the parents is thus a function of the overall total number of leave days provided to new parents, individual family considerations and societal mindsets and norms about the roles of fathers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I fully agree with Ms Carrie Tan's point that we need shifts in societal mindsets and norms so that couples can best decide how they can jointly take care of their new child without preconceived stereotypes on caregiving.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In addition, workplace support is also important as it impacts the willingness of fathers to take leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We should also not forget the very important point that Minister of State Gan Siow Huang has made with regard to FWAs, as its availability can make a big difference to how caregiving arrangements can be sorted out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   A few weeks ago, I attended a dialogue session on Singapore Women's Development organised by the Singapore Federation of Chinese Clan Associations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As housewives and caregivers, several female participants shared concerns about their financial situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The family is the cornerstone of our society, and women play a crucial role in the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Around us, we see many women juggling both work and family commitments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also many women who are homemakers, working hard for their families over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We know deep in our hearts that a warm, harmonious family provides a spiritual harbour for family members to return to after a hard day's work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With their tenderness, patience and resilience, women provide emotional support and assistance to family members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Their contributions are not directly captured in our GDP, but we know that their contributions have enabled their husbands and children to succeed and helped build strong and happy families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Every family is unique and the couple will share responsibilities according to their situation, in a way that is acceptable and suitable to both parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government respects every family's choice and does its best to create a fair, harmonious environment and formulate pro-family policies that keep up with the times, to provide relevant support to families based on their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Family members can also show their care for their loved ones by tapping on the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to help them save more for old age.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These top-ups to their Central Provident Fund (CPF) accounts are eligible for tax relief.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While the Government does step in to help families in need, we should not intervene in a manner that is too intrusive, such as to monetise the relationship between a couple through mandating a spousal allowance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will cause spousal relationships to deteriorate, turning it into monetary transactions, with the Government acting as the arbiter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Wives and housewives often say that they hope to be appreciated by their families and that their contributions should not be taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They also hope to be financially self-sufficient, to take care of their own needs in old age when they are unable to work, instead of relying on children who may need to take care of their own families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Besides expressing our appreciation, caring for and respecting family members, we can also consider topping up their CPF accounts which will be matched by the Government.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will give homemakers greater financial assurance for their future needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together with contributions from the community and families, we can make Singapore a fairer and more inclusive society for our future generations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In English): Lastly, I would like to address questions raised on elective egg freezing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since the announcement has gone out, I have received many emails from women who welcome the choice but are concerned about the age limit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui had also suggested to extend the age limit to 40 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some ask why this is so since they are a woman's own eggs rather than a donor's eggs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The reason is because it is founded on similar current international scientific evidence and professional consensus, which is that egg quality tends to decline significantly after 35 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are making a big move with regard to providing the choice of elective egg freezing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government had taken time to study the issue because there are differing voices and views and concerns about elective egg freezing, such as whether we are encouraging women to put off marriage and parenthood when women face the hard truths and the scientific facts of the biological clock.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government has the responsibility to let citizens know factually what the medical odds are of conceiving with frozen eggs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The further we push out the age range, the more the success rates fall.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have to be honest with our women because the procedure is invasive, it takes a toll on the women both physically and emotionally, and also costs the patient recurrent costs for storage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But that said, we recognise Miss Cheng Li Hui's point that many women only start thinking about fertility and egg freezing in their 30s.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For women who missed the local criteria slightly and who wish to appeal, they may seek the Assisted Reproduction practitioner's assistance to appeal on their behalf.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More details will be provided to the AR Centres in due course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Miss Cheng Li Hui that, with more conversations, there is more awareness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I hope that this move to allow women to have the choice to freeze their eggs has also created some awareness and space for conversations about fertility health and cause women to think about these issues earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships is also starting to raise awareness on this matter to encourage couples to discuss and check their fertility early.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is also looking into supporting couples with ready access to evidence-based fertility health information to empower them to make fertility decisions and seek help if needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Janet Ang spoke about her concern that younger women will now choose to postpone childbearing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will highlight the limitations, the risks involved and that aged parenthood has its own challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are grateful for the diverse feedback received.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And we have had to navigate trade-offs, balance concerns while identifying the best way forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More importantly, it is time now for us to take action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Let us come together and work collectively to build a fairer and more inclusive society, where men and women partner each other as equals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There has been a marathon debate, feels almost like childbirth, but with epidural.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because, fortunately, support for the Motion is unanimous, whether from PAP or Opposition Members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I want to thank the Workers' Party, the PSP for speaking in support, even if we may not agree on everything.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is surely a good outcome for women and for Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In my opening speech, I encouraged Members to focus on two key elements of the Motion being debated: how to catalyse further collective action; and how to realise greater equality of partnership between women and men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I appreciate all Members who spoke and for contributing their proposals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On catalysing collective action, Members like Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Abdul Samad highlighted the importance of tripartism.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Poh Li San emphasised the media's role in shifting mindsets and Mr Darryl David underscored the need for a whole-of-society approach to uplift women.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On realising more equal partnerships, Members like Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, Mr Louis Ng and Mr Louis Chua highlighted the role of men in caregiving and how institutional arrangements must encourage it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My colleagues in Government have also responded to specific comments by Members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To suggestions by Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Melvin Yong to bring it forward, Minister of State Gan Siow Huang has highlighted that, in fact, MOM will promote greater adoption of the existing tripartite standards to boost momentum for the eventual implementation of the guidelines.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On protection against violence and harms, Ms Sylvia Lim made suggestions concerning family violence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Minister Shanmugam has outlined the holistic response that MHA is taking.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Responding to Ms Hany Soh and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann has elaborated on how the Sunlight Alliance for Action will promote greater awareness of online harms and provide more holistic support to advocates in the community, as well as victims.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Tin Pei Ling called on the Government to increase the capacity for respite care.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In response, Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam shared MOH's commitment to make it more accessible and affordable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's suggestion, Minister of State Low Yen Ling shared how the Government is working with community partners to strengthen peer support networks to better support caregivers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On changing mindsets, we absolutely agree with Ms Ng Ling Ling, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Leon Perera, Dr Shahira Abdullah and Ms Carrie Tan that it is foundational.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We also agree with Ms Janet Ang and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that more women are ready today for leadership roles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli has declared his support and his Ministry's active interventions on this front.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, Minister Ong Ye Kung underscored society's collective duty.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some questions take time to consider, like those raised by Ms Hazel Poa on mandating CPF top-ups for caregivers by their spouses or those by Miss Rachel Ong and Mr Gerald Giam on legislating parental or family care leave.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, should paternity and maternity leave benefits be equalised to better reflect the desire for equal sharing of responsibilities between fathers and mothers in caring for their newborns?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But as Minister of State Sun Xueling has pointed out, societal norms constrain men from fully utilising existing leave provisions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: More leave provided does not automatically lead to more leave taken.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At which point would mindsets have shifted sufficiently such that the equal provision of parental leave would, in fact, result in the equal sharing of responsibilities?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Every now and then, we should revisit them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And even if we do not, Mr Louis Ng will make sure that we do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Like the subject of elective egg freezing, which Miss Cheng Li Hui championed for years, it takes time to develop deeper understanding and to build consensus on what is right for our women and our society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, the White Paper distils the views of Singaporeans over the year-long conversations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As early as September last year, Prime Minister Lee had outlined its key recommendations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In truth, advancing the cause of women's development is a journey without end.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In every generation, we must find new ways to elevate women.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We cross each new milestone in the hope of going further to reach the next.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As we commit ourselves to action, it is also worth asking what today's debate has achieved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I suggest to Members that its greatest contribution is in upholding the values we hold dear as a society and which will serve as our North Star as we seek out the next milestones in women's development.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first and foremost has to be the equality of women and men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: History is replete with examples of women being subjugated by men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In ancient Athens, widely regarded as the birthplace of democracy, women received little education.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They lived in their own quarters separate from men – maybe it is for their own protection – and were confined to household duties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Not that these were unimportant, but women were otherwise excluded in society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even towards the end of the European Age of Enlightenment, French philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau argued that women did not need to be educated to the same extent as men since their main duty in life was to please their husbands and educate their sons.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead, we reaffirm the value of equality between women and men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: No one is left in doubt that Singapore women should have equal opportunities to pursue their aspirations as much as men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The tone of this debate has also upheld the value of partnership.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Workplace fairness, FWAs and caregiver support benefit women as well as men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We aim to ensure that advances for one do not diminish the other.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead, it strengthens boys and men when our mothers, sisters, wives and daughters are uplifted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In a true partnership, both gain from each other's growth.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the same way, the partnership between the Government and the community at large has helped to bring about positive change for Singapore women.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A third and essential value underpinning equality and partnership is that of mutual respect between men and women.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a society, we should respect women's place in it and honour their contributions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Equally, we respect men's choice and ability to support women in their capacities as fathers, husbands, brothers, bosses, colleagues and friends.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mutual respect shapes our attitudes and beliefs about women and men.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They reach the corners of our minds that laws, regulations, guidelines and practices will never fully reach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They determine the culture and norms within which we all live.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They move our hearts and spur us to action so that supporting women is a "want to do" rather than "have to do".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At its core, respect means that women should not be exploited.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Rather, women deserve to be recognised for their contributions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Women deserve to be respected as equal partners in society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These core values of equality, partnership and mutual respect must endure with every step we take in advancing women's interests.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is now up to us to put our values once again into action.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In Mandarin):   Over the past decades, Singapore women have achieved exceptional progress in various fields.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This White Paper is, therefore, about honouring Singapore women and recognising their place in society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We honour them for fighting the battles to be seen and heard, recognised and valued.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We honour them for their unyielding spirit that has led to many triumphs over adversity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We honour them for their unwavering commitment to blazing a trail and paving the way for other women to succeed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The value of the White Paper goes beyond legislative and policy changes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Through a whole-of-nation plan of action, it aims to achieve further progress for Singapore women by putting the values we hold dear into action.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In English): Sir, at the start of the debate, I described my own struggles as a working woman, highlighting the men who were my staunchest allies: my husband, my father, father in-law, my brothers, my bosses and my colleagues.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Equally, many women in my life have been instrumental.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My popo, a widow from the time she was in her late 30s, began to educate me well before I started school.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Riding on a little trishaw in Joo Chiat to visit her former midwife and her relatives, popo pointed to all the signboards on the shops that we passed to teach me to recognise Chinese characters.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thanks to popo's spirit of adventure, I served as her English-speaking travel guide on trips abroad and cultivated my own curiosity about the world.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My mother, a former Police officer, held court at work and at home.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: She is not one to easily take no for an answer nor will she ever retreat to helplessness in any situation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because of mom, I learnt how to juggle my studies, my passion for basketball as well as preparing meals daily for my younger brothers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My mother-in-law, who had raised seven children on a shoe string and cared for half a dozen more grandchildren, graciously helped with our late additions when they arrived.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Without her support in those critical first years, I would easily have given up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My twin daughters, whose wide-eyed wonder and joyful encouragement, inspired mommy to finally get a driver's licence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My reliable helper of 23 years whom I always introduced as "the children's real mother", won her 10-year fight against breast cancer and is still with us.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Khoo Seok Lin, Director of Planning in EDB in the 1990s, who stuck her neck out to recommend a scholarship for me because she believed there was room in the organisation for both me and the only other scholarship recipient that year – a man.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Shirley Chen and Anna Chan who, as my bosses, showed how women can assert our views with conviction and grace.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My personal assistants (PAs) and security officers at different times – Patricia, Alice, Wendy, Chris, Jeya, Alicia, Eunice, Iris, Jocelyn, Silver and Charlene.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am so blessed to have them in my life because they make every day better for me.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My best friends forever since childhood, my newfound sisters in the Labour Movement and PAP Women's Wing, with whom I share laughter and tears.
